titulo: The hammer sentence, and the card that says it for you
subtitulo: An allergy is not a preference — it needs a sentence that cannot be softened and a written card that survives a loud kitchen
cena: The waiter is nodding warmly at something you said, and you cannot tell whether they understood the word or just the tone.
frasePiso: Say the word allergia, name the food, and do not decorate it. Then hand over the card.

steps.pt: The last part taught you to subtract politely. This one is different. An allergy is not a preference and must not sound like one.
Lead with the word allergia. It is the word that changes what happens in the kitchen, so it goes first, not last.

steps.es: Ho un'allergia alle arachidi. È grave.
steps.pinyin: oh oo-nal-ler-JEE-a AL-le a-RA-kee-dee. eh GRA-ve
steps.pt: I have a peanut allergy. It is serious.
steps.tts: Ho un'allergia alle arachidi. È grave.

steps.promptPt: Say it before ordering, not after. Name it and say it is serious. Speak now.
steps.es: Ho un'allergia alle arachidi. È grave.
steps.pinyin: oh oo-nal-ler-JEE-a AL-le a-RA-kee-dee. eh GRA-ve
steps.pt: I have a peanut allergy. It is serious.

steps.es: Ho capito. Lo dico in cucina.
steps.tts: Ho capito. Lo dico in cucina.

steps.pt: Lo dico in cucina is the answer you want. A warm nod without it means the message stopped at the table.

steps.promptPt: You did not hear the kitchen mentioned. Ask them to tell the kitchen. Speak now.
steps.es: Può dirlo in cucina, per favore?
steps.pinyin: pwoh DEER-lo een koo-CHEE-na per fa-VO-re
steps.pt: Can you tell the kitchen, please?
steps.tts: Può dirlo in cucina, per favore?

steps.pt: Now the card. Write it before the trip, in Italian, on paper and on your phone. Paper works when the battery does not.

steps.promptPt: Hand over the written card instead of repeating yourself. Speak now.
Ask directly whether the dish contains it. Speak now.

steps.es: Questo no, ma è fritto nello stesso olio.
steps.pt: Not this one, but it's fried in the same oil.
steps.tts: Questo no, ma è fritto nello stesso olio.
steps.acao: Change dish. Same oil is a real risk, not a technicality.

steps.pt: That answer is the good one. Same oil, same board, same water is the risk the menu never prints.

steps.promptPt: Ask what there is with none of it at all, using the frame from B12. Speak now.
Say what happens if you eat it, in four words. Speak now.
steps.pt: I would have to go to hospital.

steps.promptPt: The worst case. Ask them to call an ambulance. Speak now.
The plate has arrived. Confirm once before the first bite. Speak now.
steps.pt: Sorry, is this the one without peanuts?

steps.es: Ho un'allergia alle arachidi. È grave. Può dirlo in cucina, per favore?
steps.pinyin: oh oo-nal-ler-JEE-a AL-le a-RA-kee-dee. eh GRA-ve. pwoh DEER-lo een koo-CHEE-na per fa-VO-re
steps.pt: Shadow the hammer sentence and the kitchen follow-up.
steps.tts: Ho un'allergia alle arachidi. È grave. Può dirlo in cucina, per favore?

steps.pt: B13 done. Allergia first, è grave second, the card third, and one confirmation before the first bite.

secoes.titulo: Swap the food, keep the sentence
secoes.corpo: Arachidi is the rehearsal ingredient. Replace it with yours and the structure does not move: ho un'allergia a…, è grave.

secoes.titulo: Why è grave earns its place
secoes.corpo: Without it, an allergy can be filed alongside a dislike. Two words move it from the waiter's memory into the kitchen's process, and they cost nothing to say.

secoes.titulo: Write the card before you fly
secoes.corpo: One short line in Italian naming the allergen and the consequence, on paper and on the phone. It survives noise, accents, a shift change and a dead battery — none of which your pronunciation does.

EU rules require food businesses to make allergen information available, including in restaurants, which is why questo piatto contiene…? is a question staff are prepared for rather than an unusual demand.

permissao: You are allowed to be blunt about this one. Everything else in the course is about sounding easy to deal with; an allergy is the exception where clarity beats warmth, and no Italian waiter will think worse of you for saying it plainly twice.
espelho: Anyone with an allergy has had the moment at home where a server nodded, repeated it back correctly, and the dish still came out wrong. The card is not distrust of Italy — it is the same insurance you would want in your own city.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You state your allergy, the waiter smiles warmly and says something reassuring, and moves on without writing anything down.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: They understood — it would be rude to raise it again.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: Warmth is the default register of Italian service and it does not signal that the message reached the kitchen. The thing you are listening for is not friendliness, it is a reference to the kitchen — lo dico in cucina.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: If the kitchen was not mentioned, ask può dirlo in cucina? and hand over the written card. Then confirm once when the plate arrives.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: The information ends up where the food is actually made, rather than stopping at the table where it was received kindly.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not a reason to repeat yourself a fourth time after the kitchen has clearly been told — at that point checking the plate on arrival is the useful move, not saying it again.
